subject.title: Feature request: per-pattern session maintenance retention rules

question: Should OpenClaw add user-configurable ordered per-pattern or per-type session-retention rules, or keep retention policy limited to current global thresholds plus narrow built-in lifecycle cleanup?
rationale: The missing capability is clear in source, docs, and release code, but implementing it changes destructive cleanup behavior and adds a public config surface that repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Design a canonical retention policy
options.body: Specify matcher grammar, precedence with protected/preserved sessions, dry-run output, docs, and upgrade behavior before queuing implementation.

options.title: Keep built-in special cases only
options.body: Continue fixing concrete ephemeral-session accumulation cases with narrow built-in cleanup paths and close this broader feature direction as not planned.

options.title: Split to narrower issues
options.body: Use the open per-label, preserveKeys, and terminology issues for focused design slices while deferring general pattern rules.

recommendation.title: Design a canonical retention policy
recommendation.body: Specify matcher grammar, precedence with protected/preserved sessions, dry-run output, docs, and upgrade behavior before queuing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current unified session maintenance contract and docs, making them the strongest history-backed owner for deciding whether to expand that contract.
